sourcedFrom: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: One Savage book covers the MSR series, and it flags two places where the large-frame MSR-10 differs from the rest. The strip itself is the standard AR sequence.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber seen empty, safety on
steps.action: Drop the magazine, lock the bolt back and put your eye on the empty chamber, then set the two-position safety and close the bolt. Savage opens the strip from a CLOSED bolt, not a locked-back one, so the last thing you do is let it run forward on an empty chamber. Do not skip closing it — with the bolt back the takedown pin will move but the upper will not swing clear of the carrier. Seeing an empty chamber and feeling the safety detent are the two confirmations; neither substitutes for the other.
steps.caution: Parts are under tension. Keep your fingers and eyes away from springs and moving parts and always wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning.
steps.quote: After confirming the firearm is unloaded (as detailed in SECTION 4) and the SAFETY is on, close the BOLT.
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 1, p.12

steps.title: Know what your barrel is marked
steps.action: Read the cartridge designation stamped on the barrel and match it to the ammunition in front of you. This one manual covers the whole MSR series across several chamberings, so the book cannot tell you what you are holding — the barrel can. Get this wrong and the round either will not chamber or will chamber something it should not.
steps.prose: This is the manual telling you, in its own words, that it is written to a series rather than to one gun.
steps.quote: Each model of firearm in the Savage Arms MSR series is chambered and marked for a specific cartridge.
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 3 Calibers & Ammunition, p.7

steps.title: Takedown pin right, then pivot pin right
steps.action: Push the takedown pin from the left until it stops on the right side, then do the same to the pivot pin. Both are captivated and will not come free — expect them to stop with a positive check rather than fall out, and do not lever at them looking for more travel. With the takedown pin out the rear hinges open; with the pivot pin out the two halves separate entirely. Support both receivers as they part so they never slam together.
steps.caution: Always control the movement of the UPPER RECEIVER and LOWER RECEIVER, never allowing them to forcibly contact each other.
steps.quote: Push the TAKEDOWN PIN to the right (it is captivated so that it won't come out completely
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 2, p.12

steps.title: Carrier out on a half-drawn handle
steps.action: Draw the charging handle back roughly halfway — just far enough to walk the bolt carrier out of its tunnel — then lift the carrier free of the upper receiver. Going all the way back is the common mistake: it runs the handle out of its own slot before the carrier has cleared, and the two jam on each other. Half way, carrier out, then deal with the handle.
steps.prose: The carrier is what actually leaves first; the handle is only carrying it back far enough to be grasped.
steps.quote: Pull back on the CHARGING HANDLE approximately half way.
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, steps 4-5, p.13

steps.title: Charging handle down, then out
steps.action: Push down on the charging handle so its tabs drop clear of the slot in the receiver, then slide it out the back. It only releases at one point along its travel, so if it will not come, move it a fraction fore or aft and press down again rather than forcing it.
steps.quote: Push down on the CHARGING HANDLE to disengage it from the slot
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 6, p.13

steps.title: Side charger? Then there are six more steps
steps.action: Look at your upper. If it carries a side charging handle, Savage routes you through six extra steps with a 5/64" and a 1/8" Allen wrench before you go on; if it does not, skip them entirely. This is the manual branching on hardware, not on model name, so decide it by looking at the rifle rather than by what the box said.
steps.quote: For models incorporating a SIDE CHARGING HANDLE (see FIGURE 15), follow steps 7 through 12.  For models without a SIDE CHARGING HANDLE, please skip down to step 13.
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, branch note before step 7, p.13

steps.title: Buffer retainer down, buffer and spring out
steps.action: With the hammer still cocked, press the buffer retainer down and let the buffer and action spring come out of the tube. Keep a hand in front of them — the spring is compressed and will follow the buffer out. Inspect both as they come; a kinked spring or a chewed buffer face is the usual reason a rifle short-strokes.
steps.quote: With the HAMMER still cocked, press down on the BUFFER RETAINER (see FIGURE 26) so that the BUFFER can be removed.
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 18, p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Upper and lower are apart, the carrier group and charging handle are out, and the buffer and action spring are out of the tube. That is the whole published strip and Savage draws a hard line right here. The bolt carrier group comes apart further and that is on the Deep Clean path; nothing beyond it is documented.
steps.quote: Do not disassemble your Savage MSR series beyond this point.
steps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, bound after step 19, p.15
steps.warn: Damage to or alteration of the BOLT ASSEMBLY or any component/assembly can affect the safe operation of your firearm, and result in injury and gun damage.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin out of the carrier and set it somewhere it will not roll away. It is a split pin and it is meant to stay split — do not spread the legs to make it easier next time, and never substitute a hardware-store cotter pin for it. That pin is the only thing keeping the firing pin in the carrier under recoil.
deepSteps.caution: Do not try to open the split end of the FIRING PIN RETAINING PIN or replace it with a standard Cotter Pin.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the FIRING PIN RETAINING PIN from the BOLT CARRIER
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 13, p.14

deepSteps.title: Firing pin AND its spring
deepSteps.action: Tip the carrier and let the firing pin out the back — and on the MSR-10 expect a firing pin spring to come with it. Savage names that difference explicitly for this model. Account for the spring before you set the parts down; it is small, it is dark, and it is not on the small-frame rifle you may be used to.
deepSteps.prose: Remove the firing pin from the bolt carrier as step 14 directs, then look for the spring.
deepSteps.quote: The MSR-10 also has a FIRING PIN SPRING.
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, note under step 14, p.14

deepSteps.title: Cam pin — read Savage's carve-out before you rotate
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt head rearward, then look at what Savage wrote about the cam pin: the quarter-turn rotation is prescribed for all models EXCEPT the AR-10 pattern, which is the large-frame family this .308 rifle belongs to. Try the pin gently. If it lifts straight out without rotating, that is the large-frame arrangement and forcing a rotation into it is how cam pins get galled.
deepSteps.quote: Push the BOLT HEAD rearward and the rotate the CAM PIN (on all models except the AR-10) as shown in FIGURE 23.
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 15, p.14
deepSteps.warn: Savage names the AR-10 pattern as the exception to this rotation and does not print a separate large-frame step. Where the book is silent, do not invent the motion — lift gently and let the part tell you.

deepSteps.title: Cam pin out
deepSteps.action: Lift the cam pin straight up and out of the carrier. It only clears in one rotational position, so if it will not lift, rotate it back a quarter turn and try again rather than pulling harder. Straight up — angling it binds the pin in its slot.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the CAM PIN by pulling it straight up
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 16, p.14

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Grip the bolt firmly and draw it straight forward out of the carrier. Everything left in your hand — bolt, cam pin, firing pin, retaining pin — is what actually gets scrubbed; the carrier body is the easy part.
deepSteps.quote: Grasping the BOLT ASSEMBLY firmly, pull it straight out of the BOLT CARRIER
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 5 Disassembly, step 17, p.15

deepSteps.title: Scrub the bolt, cam pin and firing pin
deepSteps.action: Clean the three parts that actually see combustion gas: the bolt, the cam pin and the firing pin. Carbon on the cam pin bearing surfaces is what makes a carrier feel gritty, and carbon in the firing pin channel is what makes a rifle light primers.
deepSteps.quote: Thoroughly clean the BOLT ASSEMBLY, CAM PIN, and FIRING PIN
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 6 Cleaning, step 3, p.15

deepSteps.title: Bolt face, and prove the extractor and ejector move
deepSteps.action: Work a Q-tip around the bolt face and under the extractor claw, then press the ejector plunger and the extractor and watch both spring back. A sticky ejector is a stovepipe waiting to happen and you will only find it here, with the bolt in your hand.
deepSteps.quote: Using a Q-Tip® (or equivalent), thoroughly clean the BOLT FACE, assuring the EXTRACTOR and EJECTOR move freely
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 6 Cleaning, step 4, p.16

deepSteps.title: Thumb on the hammer when you let it down
deepSteps.action: When the action goes back together and you drop the hammer, ride it down with your thumb rather than letting it fall. Left to itself it slams into the bolt release and beats it up. Keep your thumb where the hammer can pinch it, not where it can trap it.
deepSteps.quote: Always support the HAMMER with your thumb when uncocking the action (pulling the trigger) so that it doesn't slam forward and damage the BOLT RELEASE.
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms MSR Series Instruction Manual — MSR Series Instruction Manual — SECTION 6 Oiling, warning, p.16

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Clean the bolt, cam pin and firing pin thoroughly
Q-tip the bolt face and confirm the extractor and ejector move freely
Clean the inside of the bolt carrier, removing any residue

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Lay the upper receiver horizontally and run the correct-caliber bore cleaner through
Look down the barrel and confirm it is clear of obstructions and free of nicks, rust or pitting
Apply a very light coat of gun lubricant — a thin film is enough

cleaning.name: BUFFER & SPRING
tasks: Wipe the buffer and action spring with a soft cloth
Inspect both for excessive wear or deformation before they go back in

reassembly: Reassemble per the applicable section of the manual, in the reverse of the order the parts came off.
Support the hammer with your thumb when you uncock the action so it cannot slam the bolt release.
Verify that the two-position safety is operational as explained in SECTION 2.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty, cycle the charging handle and confirm the bolt runs and locks; then check the two-position safety operates as the manual describes before handling.
